function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

On Windows, we can list installed programs via registry or via wmic product get name. But wmic might be slow. We could use powershell: Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Select-Object Name. Or use Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*.

We can search for known VPN names: "OpenVPN", "Cisco AnyConnect", "FortiClient", "Palo Alto GlobalProtect", "NordVPN", "ExpressVPN", "Tunnelblick" (Mac). But it's Windows. So we can query installed programs and see if any contain "vpn" or known vendor names.

We can run a command like:

powershell -Command "Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\* | Select-Object DisplayName"

But maybe simpler: wmic product get name. That returns all installed products. Then parse output for known VPN names.

We can also check services: net start | findstr /I "vpn".

But the question: "is any vpn is installed". Likely they want a yes/no answer. We can run a command to list installed programs and filter for "vpn". Let's do:

But wmic may not return all. Alternatively, use PowerShell:

But we can combine with findstr.

Let's propose a command: powershell -Command "Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\* | Where-Object {$_.DisplayName -match '(?i)vpn'} | Select-Object DisplayName"
